electric-iris.$description: Electric Iris — Violet supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

ink-black.$description: Ink Black — Primary text, dark secondary buttons, icon strokes, hairline borders — warmer than pure black, reads as ink rather than void

paper-white.$description: Paper White — Card surfaces, elevated panels, button text on dark fills, page sections that need to lift off the pale-blue canvas

chalk-blue.$description: Chalk Blue — Dominant page canvas — a barely-there blue tint that prevents the page from feeling clinical and ties the scattered blue shapes to the background

frost-blue.$description: Frost Blue — Secondary surface wash, input field backgrounds, footer tint — a step deeper than the canvas to create soft layering without shadows

carbon.$description: Carbon — Dark supporting neutral for text, icons, and strong contrast. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

marker-red.$description: Marker Red — Decorative shape fill — the large red semicircle, star bursts, and accent blobs scattered through the decorative layer

hi-yellow.$description: Hi-Yellow — Decorative shape fill — the yellow pentagon and sunny accents in the cutout composition; also used as a section wash behind featured content

powder-sky.$description: Powder Sky — Decorative shape fill — soft powder-blue circles and cloud forms in the scattered cutout scene

bubblegum-pink.$description: Bubblegum Pink — Red supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis.

jelly-green.$description: Jelly Green — Decorative shape fill — green triangle accents in the scattered cutout scene

sunbeam.$description: Sunbeam — Decorative shape fill — a slightly warmer yellow variant for layering against Hi-Yellow in the cutout composition

haas-grot-disp.$description: Display and headings only — the geometric grotesque has a sturdy, slightly condensed skeleton that holds 92px hero lines without losing legibility; weight stays at 400 because the tight letter-spacing (-0.03em at the largest sizes) does the heavy-lifting, not bold weight

haas-grot-text.$description: Body, navigation, buttons, and smaller UI text — the text cut of the same family tuned for readability at small sizes with looser tracking than the display companion

martian-mono.$description: Promotional ticker text, tag labels, and code-flavored micro-copy — a monospaced voice used sparingly for editorial texture, not for entire paragraphs
